turns.prompt_text: is there an app in the Play Store so that I can use it as a stud finder by tapping the wall and creating a sound image of the wall?
turns.response_html:
No, there isn't a reliable app that uses sound/tapping to create an image of your wall. Standard "stud finder" apps on the Play Store actually use your phone's magnetometer to detect metal (like nails or screws) rather than density or sound.

Better Alternatives

  • Magnetic Apps: If you have drywall, apps like "Stud Finder" or "Metal Detector" can help you find the screws in the studs, but they won't show a "sound image."
  • Specialized Hardware: For a true visual "image" of what's inside the wall (pipes, wires, and studs), you would need a device like Walabot DIY, which plugs into your phone and uses radio frequency.
  • Manual Method: You can use the "knock method" without an app—listen for the sound to change from hollow to solid—then verify by looking for small vertical bumps or dimples in the drywall paint where the screws are located.

turns.prompt_text: Yeah, but why wouldn't you be able to use the knock method with your phone to upgrade it so that your phone records the different decibel levels as you walk around the wall?
turns.response_html:
While that sounds like a clever use of acoustic fingerprinting, several technical hurdles keep it from being a reality on the Play Store:

  • Background Noise: Phone microphones are designed to pick up voices, not subtle vibrations. Ambient noise—even a car driving by or an AC unit—can easily drown out the slight change in frequency between a hollow space and a stud.
  • Hardware Fragmentation: Unlike a human ear, which is relatively consistent, Android phones use hundreds of different microphone types. Calibration would be a nightmare because every phone "hears" the wall differently.
  • Acoustic Complexity: Walls aren't just hollow or solid; layers of paint, insulation, and different drywall thicknesses create "echoes" that are difficult for standard phone processors to map into a clean visual image.

In short, the magnetic sensor in your phone is far more reliable because metal screws have a distinct, measurable effect that sound waves just don't offer to a tiny mobile microphone.
